judged_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save, using the association delete as the real mutation and wrapping it in a save that cannot meaningfully fail — validation-less dead control flow. adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` as the real mutation, followed by `if group.save ... else ...` (new method near bottom of controller). Since `delete` removes the join record directly, `group.save` is largely redundant and is unlikely to fail due to this operation; also the code does not check the return value of `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which can be 0 if the user wasn’t a member), so the endpoint still returns `success_json`. This is a valid, diff-grounded API/semantics concern, but it’s not a clearly verifiable correctness defect because idempotent “remove” semantics may intentionally return success even when nothing was removed, and `save` is not strictly provably dead from the diff alone.
